Expressed in **ascending order** in radians, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions to the equation  $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-0.8,$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$   are

$x≈$
{{field-1}}, $\,x≈$
{{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-0.8)=-0.927\,295…≈-0.9273\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $x=-0.9273$ is not in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ To get the first solution that's within the required domain, we need to find an angle that's coterminal with $-0.9273.$ To do this, we simply add $2\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-0.9273+2\pi ≈5.3559\end{aligned}
$$

 

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=0.9273.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=0.9273.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951962/assets/942d3d727557ee280b93b212e856f4a696bcf06438944299fd6596dfb5b147f4.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +0.9273 \\  & ≈4.0689\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are  

$$
x≈4.1,\,x≈5.4.
$$
